findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be constructed
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler and only has `pass`, but StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Instantiating it raises TypeError. It is still wired as MetricAlertFire.detector_handler, and Detector.detector_handler does `group_type.detector_handler(self)` with no try/except in process_detectors, so any detector whose type resolves to metric_alert_fire crashes the whole batch. The previous handler was a concrete evaluate() that returned no results. Implement the abstract methods (even as explicit stubs) or keep it on DetectorHandler until the stateful implementation exists.

findings.title: Group-key evaluation test expects the wrong occurrence
findings.body: TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe builds the expected IssueOccurrence with group_key "val1" (and value 6) but calls evaluate_group_key_value with group_key "group_key" and value 10. The handler fingerprints the occurrence from the evaluated group key, so the returned DetectorEvaluationResult cannot equal that expected result. The assertion is wrong and will fail, and it does not lock the new build_occurrence_and_event_data inputs.

findings.title: Expected occurrences are built with the wrong value
findings.body: Several new assertions build the expected occurrence with a hardcoded value of 6 that is not the value under test: test_state_results_multi_group uses group_2=10 but builds occurrence_2 with 6 (and asserts that payload to Kafka); TestEvaluate.test_results_on_change evaluates 100; TestEvaluate.test_dedupe evaluates 8. build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores value, so the tests pass without checking that the new hook received the packet value. A later change that includes value in the occurrence will fail for the wrong reason, and a bug that forwards the wrong value will not be caught. Build each expected occurrence with the same group key and value the code evaluates.

findings.title: evaluate() docstring still says it returns a list
findings.body: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate now returns dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult], which is the contract change in this PR, but the docstring still says it "returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult". Callers and subclass authors will follow the wrong shape.
